lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
- Cut the signal's daily turnover from 34% to 21% with a cost-aware position smoother, keeping 90% of gross returns and lowering estimated slippage by a third.
- Confirmed the forecast gain over the nested HAR-RV baseline with standard Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices.
- Joining 120 microstructure features point-in-time across six venues, deduplicating late prints and versioning each schema, built a feature store the team reused in two later projects.
- Annualized the signal's daily Sharpe ratio by multiplying it by 252 before reporting it to the desk.
- Documented the backtest assumptions, transaction-cost model and known failure regimes in the desk's research wiki, which the next intern cohort used to onboard in their first week.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Built the lab's simulation pipeline on the shared cluster, cutting a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours, with every run reproducible from its seed and configuration file.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.

- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation while maintaining the lab's shared cluster, organizing the weekly reading group and grading for two courses, which was downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Cut forecast error from 0.20 to 0.15, a 33% improvement, by adding realized-volatility features and an asymmetric loss.
- Improved the model's directional hit rate by 6% on 30 equity indices, from 52% to 58%, with a temporal convolutional model.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Placed 41st of 2,900 teams with a gradient-boosting ensemble on 300 engineered features, finishing in the top 2% of the private leaderboard.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Wrote the team's feature-selection script using permutation importance, trimming 900 candidate features to 300 without losing validation score.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: The education entries are not in newest-first order.
items.because: The review says this breaks the ordering used elsewhere and makes the timeline less consistent to scan.

items.says: The Sunrise Bakery entry takes more than one line without advancing the quantitative-research direction.
items.because: Its two bullets take space from more relevant research and technical work.

items.says: The labour-budget claim gives no figure showing how closely spending matched the budget.
The past-tense verb may make an ongoing responsibility sound completed.
The past-tense verb may make an ongoing responsibility sound completed.
The causal link between stock counts and orders and the reduction in unsold bread is unclear.
items.because: Counts do not reduce unsold bread on their own, and supplier orders usually concern inputs rather than finished bread.

items.says: Standard Diebold–Mariano tests do not provide usual valid inference for the nested-baseline comparison.
items.because: Their null distribution can differ for nested forecast models, so the tests may not reliably establish the claimed gain.

items.says: “The forecast gain” does not say what improved or by how much.
items.because: Without the measured improvement, a reader cannot judge its practical importance.

items.says: “Standard” is filler before the named tests.
“Joining” does not form a grammatical construction with “built” as written.
items.because: The opening phrase lacks a grammatical link to the main verb.

items.says: The feature-store outcome is buried beneath implementation details.
items.because: The bullet lists methods before saying the team reused the result.

items.says: Multiplying a daily Sharpe ratio by 252 is not the standard annualization.
items.because: Under the usual uncorrelated-returns assumption, the multiplier is √252.

items.says: The reporting detail does not show what the calculation contributed to a desk assessment or decision.
items.because: Without an outcome or reported value, it reads as a routine task rather than a research contribution.

items.says: The onboarding outcome is buried after the documentation detail.
The first-person pronoun “my” does not belong in this résumé bullet.
The teaching rating lacks the number of student responses behind it.
The package description does not name the technical work it contains.
items.because: Its application is clear, but not the statistical or implementation skill contributed.

items.says: The package-download result is buried after unrelated duties.
items.because: The reader must pass through the cluster, reading-group and grading duties before reaching the result.

items.says: “Which” has an unclear referent.
items.because: It follows a list of duties, making it less clear that the downloads refer to the package.

items.says: Unrelated lab duties interrupt the package achievement and make the bullet read like a task list.
items.because: Bundling cluster maintenance, reading-group organization and grading with the release obscures the distinct contributions.

items.says: The 7% result does not say how it is summarized across the 30 indices.
“QLIKE” is specialized jargon that may slow readers unfamiliar with the metric.
The 33% improvement misstates the reduction from 0.20 to 0.15.
items.because: The reduction of 0.05 is 25% of the original 0.20 error.

items.says: The values do not identify the forecast-error metric or clearly establish the comparison.
items.because: Different metrics have different scales and interpretations, so the values alone do not let a reader judge the result.

items.says: The bullet repeats realized-volatility features already named in the preceding bullet.
items.because: Repeating the method takes space without distinguishing the error reduction.

items.says: The change from 52% to 58% is six percentage points, not a 6% increase.
items.because: The relative increase from 52% is about 11.5%.

items.says: The bullet repeats the indices and model context given in the first bullet.
items.because: Those details add length without distinguishing the directional hit-rate result.

items.says: The placement and top-2% statement report the same competition result.
items.because: A reader can infer the top-2% standing from 41st place out of 2,900 teams.

items.says: The 0.02 gap does not name the scoring metric or its scale.
The Methods skills line misspells “econometrics.”
items.because: The listed spelling, “econometircs,” is incorrect.
